LESSON: WRITING 10.5.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: PACKING AND SHOPPING LISTS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.5: Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What should one consider when grouping items in a packing list?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify ways of grouping items in packing and shopping lists
2. write a packing list for a specified event
3. recognise the importance of preparing a shopping and packing list in their everyday lives

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 10.5.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: PACKING AND SHOPPING LISTS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 10.5.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: PACKING AND SHOPPING LISTS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify ways of grouping items in packing and shopping lists

What this means
In this part you learn to identify ways of grouping items in packing and shopping lists. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify ways of grouping items in packing and shopping lists.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify ways of grouping items in packing and shopping lists. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a packing list for a specified event

What this means
In this part you learn to write a packing list for a specified event. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a packing list for a specified event.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a packing list for a specified event. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Recognise the importance of preparing a shopping and packing list in their everyday lives

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the importance of preparing a shopping and packing list in their everyday lives. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the importance of preparing a shopping and packing list in their everyday lives.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the importance of preparing a shopping and packing list in their everyday lives. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify ways of grouping items in packing and shopping lists)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists to a partner. (skill: write a packing list for a specified event)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: recognise the importance of preparing a shopping and packing list in their everyday lives)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify ways of grouping items in packing and shopping lists.
3. Practise this skill: write a packing list for a specified event.
4. Practise this skill: recognise the importance of preparing a shopping and packing list in their everyday lives.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What should one consider when grouping items in a packing list?
2. Why should a shopping list be prepared?
3. What is the importance of a packing list?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify ways of grouping items in packing and shopping lists.
5. Be able to: write a packing list for a specified event.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
